results.name: Balance Board (Version 2)
instructions: Stand on the balance board with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Shift your weight side to side by straightening one leg while lightly bending the other.
Shift your weight to the opposite side by bending the extended leg lightly and straightening the other leg.
Continue the movement in a controlled, rhythmic manner to improve balance.
tips: Focus on a point in front of you to help maintain your balance.
Start with slow movements and gradually increase the speed as you become more comfortable.
Keep your movements controlled to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
results.description: Balance Board (Version 2) is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the balance category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Glutes.

results.name: Ball Headlock Squat
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold an exercise ball to your side with one arm wrapped around it as if in a headlock. Extend the opposite arm in front of you for balance.
Begin lowering into a squat by bending your hips and knees, keeping your chest upright and back straight.
Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor and then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep the ball securely pressed to your side to maintain upper body control and tension.
Use your extended arm for balance and avoid shifting your torso.
Do not let your knees cave inward and keep them in line with your toes.
results.description: Ball Headlock Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Abdominals.

results.name: Band Bent-Over Hip Extension
instructions: Attach one end of the resistance band low on a sturdy piece of equipment and secure the other end around your right ankle. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and lean slightly forward, holding the equipment for support with both hands.
Lift your right leg straight back until parallel to the floor, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Slowly return your leg to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely attached to the equipment and your ankle to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you lift your leg back and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Maintain a slight bend in your supporting knee to protect your knee joint and lower back.
results.description: Band Bent-Over Hip Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

results.name: Band Cross Abduction
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and place the resistance band under both feet, crossing the band in front of you. Hold the handles of the band in opposite hands with arms hanging in front of your hips.
Keeping your right leg straight, lift it sideways away from your body until your leg is fully extended to the side.
Slowly lower your leg back to the starting position with control, keeping tension in the band.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely placed under your feet and properly crossed to avoid slipping.
Keep your upper body stationary and avoid leaning to the side.
Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Band Cross Abduction is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abductors (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abductors, Core.

results.name: Band Deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and place the resistance band under both feet, holding one handle of the band in each hand with your arms extended straight down, palms facing your hips.
Hinge at your hips, keeping your back straight and your knees bent, lowering your torso until it is almost parallel to the floor.
Press through your heels and extend your hips and knees to stand back up straight, bringing the handles up along your legs until you are fully upright.
Repeat the exercise for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely placed under your feet to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you stand up and inhale as you lower back down.
Use a resistance band with appropriate tension to ensure you can perform the exercise with good form.
results.description: Band Deadlift is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

results.name: Band Hip Adduction
instructions: Secure one end of the resistance band to a stable anchor and attach the other end around the ankle closest to the anchor.
Stand sideways to the anchor with your supporting leg slightly bent and your core engaged. Place your hands on hips for stability.
Sweep the banded leg inward across the front of your body while keeping your torso upright and your movement controlled.
Slowly return your leg to the starting position without letting the band pull it back, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning to either side.
Maintain a slight bend in your supporting knee for better stability. Keep the working leg straight or slightly bent throughout the movement.
Control the return phase and resist the band's pull. Use a resistance level that allows a full, controlled range of motion.
Exhale as you bring your leg inward and inhale as you return.
results.description: Band Hip Adduction is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the adductors (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Glutes, Core.

results.name: Band Kneeling Rear Kick
instructions: Kneel on all fours, on your knees and elbows, with your hands holding the handles of the band and the band looped around your right foot.
Extend your right leg straight back, keeping your foot flexed and your leg in level with your body.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement, ensuring a full contraction.
Slowly return your right leg to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you extend your leg back and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Maintain a neutral spine to avoid strain on your lower back.
Avoid rotating your hips outward; maintain square hips to the floor.
results.description: Band Kneeling Rear Kick is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

results.name: Band Leg Press
instructions: Attach a resistance band at a low-mid point on sturdy equipment. Lie on your back facing the extended cable passing over your torso, and attach your right ankle to the band using a cuff.
Bend your right knee and pull it toward your chest, while the other leg stays extended and relaxed on the floor.
Press your foot forward against the resistance, straightening your leg fully without locking the knee.
Return slowly to the starting position. Repeat for the desired repetitions, switch legs, and repeat.
tips: Engage your core to stabilize your body during the motion.
Adjust your body’s distance from the anchor to maintain consistent tension.
Ensure the band or cable has tension at the start of the movement.
results.description: Band Leg Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings, Calves.

results.name: Band Pullthrough
instructions: Stand facing away from the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart and the resistance band passing between your legs, held securely with both hands in front of you. Keep your knees slightly bent and your spine neutral.
Push your hips back while hinging at the hips, allowing your hands to move between your legs as the band stretches. Maintain a flat back and keep your arms extended.
Drive your hips forward by squeezing your glutes and return to a fully upright position while keeping your arms straight and the band under tension.
Pause briefly at the top with your glutes fully contracted, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your spine neutral and avoid rounding your back throughout the movement.
Focus on hinging at the hips rather than squatting down.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees throughout the exercise.
results.description: Band Pullthrough is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Core.

results.name: Band Single Leg Split Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the ends of a resistance band anchored under your front foot. Place your back foot on a bench behind you.
Lower your body by bending your front knee until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Push through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position, straightening your front leg.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs to work the other side.
tips: Maintain an upright torso throughout the exercise to avoid leaning forward.
Ensure your front knee stays in line with your toes to avoid putting stress on the knee joint.
Keep your weight evenly distributed on your front leg during the exercise.
results.description: Band Single Leg Split Squat is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Abdominals.
